Rule: ED HR RECORDED BEFORE DEPART (49703). This metric assesses whether the patient's heart rate was recorded prior to their departure from the ED. Rule: ED METRIC: ED INFUSIONS STOPPED (49722) This rule checks if all infusions started before the patient left the ED were recorded as stopped. If there were no infusions or if all infusions were marked as completed, the column will show "Y"; if any ED infusions lack completion documentation, it will show "N".

Rule: ED METRIC: ED LDA REMOVAL DOCUMENTED (49721) This rule uses an ED end event as input. If all LDAs placed prior to the last occurrence of the end event are removed, this column will contain a value of "Y". If an LDA was placed before the patient exited the ED and was not documented as removed, this will contain "N".

Rule: ED METRIC: NOTES SIGNED ON TIME (49719) This column contains a value of "Y" if the patient's notes were finalized within an acceptable timeframe after the patient departed the ED. The rule can be set to account for specific note types and a designated hour range post-departure, requiring at least one note of the specified types to meet these criteria, while all other notes of those types must either be completed within the timeframe or deleted; otherwise, a value of "N" is recorded in this column.

Rule: ED PAIN RECORDED BEFORE DEPART (49710) This metric assesses whether the patient's pain level was recorded prior to their departure from the ED. A value of 1 signifies that the flowsheet was completed before the patient left the ED, -1 indicates it was completed after departure, and 0 means the flowsheet was not filed during this encounter.

Rule: ED RESPIRATION RECORDED BEFORE DEPART (49704) This metric assesses whether the patient's respiration rate was recorded prior to their departure from the ED. A value of 1 signifies that the flowsheet was completed before the patient left the ED, -1 indicates it was completed after departure, and 0 means the flowsheet was not filed during this encounter.

Rule: ED PULSE OXIMETRY BEFORE DEPART (49705) This metric assesses whether pulse oximetry was recorded prior to the patient's departure from the ED. A value of 1 signifies that the flowsheet was completed before the patient left, -1 indicates it was completed after departure, and 0 means the flowsheet was not filed during this encounter.

The time can be adjusted by users in the application, which may not necessarily align with the system-audited time; for the system-recorded check-out time, refer to the CHECKOUT_AUD_DTTM column in PATIENT_ENC_7.
The Kiosk where the appointment is checked in.
The category number for the visit indicator associated with this patient encounter.
The date linked to the visit indicator as recorded by a system user during Check In.
The unique identifier for the billing system Claim record (CLM record) that is associated with charges for this visit.
Identifier for the deployment owner associated with this contact.
This item indicates the type of consent recorded for a specific encounter. It is a single-response category defined by the customer.
Comments made by the provider regarding the contact.
The date of this contact presented in a calendar format.

The value in the COPAY_COLLECTED field represents the amount entered by the user during Check In. If the facility utilizes the Registration or POS copay form, multiple copays may be collected per appointment, but this field only shows the last copay collected. Comprehensive data on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the AR copay form is used, this is the appropriate data source.

The dollar amount displayed in the COPAY_DUE field during the Check In Patient activity of the scheduling system. This amount can be either calculated by the system based on the patient's coverage benefit information or manually input by a user. The field may also be blank if no copay amount was provided at the time of the patient's check-in.
The method used to pay the copay for an appointment (e.g., through MYCHART, a kiosk).

The COPAY_PAYMENT_EXPLANATION_CATEGORY_NUMBER for this patient encounter. This field is populated only if the facility utilizes the POS copay form during check-in/check-out. Users may collect multiple copays per appointment, but this field reflects only the last copay collected for that appointment. Information on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table.

The reference number for the copay associated with this encounter during Check In, which may be a check number or credit card number. Note: If the facility utilizes the Registration or POS copay form at check-in/check-out, multiple copays may be collected per appointment, but this field only shows the last copay collected for that appointment. Information on all copays collected can be accessed in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the AR copay form is used, this is the appropriate data source.

The COPAY_SOURCE_CATEGORY_NUMBER indicates the copay source for the patient encounter. It is important to note that if the facility utilizes the Registration or POS copay form during check-in/check-out, multiple copays may be collected per appointment; however, this field only shows the last copay collected. Comprehensive data on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the AR copay form is used, this is the appropriate data source.

The COPAY_TYPE_CATEGORY_NUMBER indicates the category of copay for the patient encounter. Information on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the facility uses the AR copay form, this is the appropriate data source.
The ID number of the COVERAGE_RECORD associated with the visit at the time of scheduling or check-in. This ID may be encrypted.
This represents the name of the user who initiated the encounter.
The ID of the department associated with the encounter. If the encounter involves multiple departments, this ID corresponds to the first department in the list.
The date when the encounter was discharged.
DOWNTIME_ENCOUNTER_IDENTIFIER refers to a unique identifier for an encounter that is associated with downtime.
The kiosk workstation that handled the ED arrival.

The ENCOUNTER_DATE represents the date of the encounter, which varies based on the contact type. For surgery encounters, the date of the surgery is returned; for Hospital encounters, the appropriate date is derived from Admission/Discharge/Transfer (ADT) information. If ADT information is unavailable, the Hospital Admission date (I EPT 18850) is returned, and if that is also not found, the temporary admission date (I EPT 18846) will be provided.

The start date and time of an encounter is derived from the date in the EFFECTIVE_DATE_DT column. The time is taken from the earliest populated entry among the following fields: hospital admission time (EPT 18851), hospital temporary admission time (EPT 18847), ADT arrival time (EPT 10815), and expected admission time (EPT 10300). The SlicerDicer reporting application utilizes this column to establish the EffectiveStartDate of encounters.

The effective department ID is determined by identifying the first department with a value in the following sequence: 1) HOSPITAL_UNIT 2) PROCEDURE_PASS_DEPARTMENT (the effective department of the associated appointment or admission) 3) HOSPICE_INTAKE_DEPARTMENT 4) APPOINTMENT_DEPARTMENT.
A unique serial number assigned to this encounter, which is distinct for all patients and encounters within the system.

A flag indicating whether the encounter is closed at the time of the enterprise reporting extract. The column can contain the values Y, N, or null, where null signifies that closing the encounter is not applicable, such as in the case of a future appointment.
The unique identifier for the system user who concluded the patient encounter. This identifier may be encrypted.
The date when the patient encounter was concluded.
This column records the time when the encounter was concluded.
The ID number of the user who created the PATIENT or ENCOUNTER record.
The moment an ENCOUNTER was initiated.
The category value for the reason for freezing the encounter medication.
The category number for the encounter type associated with the encounter.

Holds the legal owning entity for the ENCOUNTER_DEPARTMENT during the encounter.
The timestamp indicating when this patient contact was created. This column is utilized for executing standard EMR validations against the source system.
Status of orders within the scheduling system.

The category value linked to the Financial Class of the encounter. Note: This item is populated solely through an interface and will not be populated if a billing system is installed.

The patient's HEAD_CIRCUMFERENCE as documented during this encounter. This field will only contain data for patients younger than the age defined in Miscellaneous Configuration. Note: This value is recorded in centimeters.
The height of the patient documented during this encounter. This field is a string and may include indicators for feet and/or inches.
The ID number associated with the hospital billing account for the encounter.
The date and time when the patient was initially admitted to the facility, placed in a bed in the ED, or confirmed for an HOV during this contact, irrespective of the patient's base patient class.
The category value indicating the type of admission for this encounter.
The date and time of discharge from the hospital for this patient contact.
Holds the Hospital License that was valid for the encounter department during the time of the encounter.
The ID number of the record that specifies the storage method for inpatient data related to the encounter.
Holds the name of the interpreter designated for an appointment when the interpreter lacks a provider record (i.e., assigned from an external source).
A flag that indicates if a patient needs an interpreter for an encounter.
This value represents the identifier of the vendor supplying the interpreter for the appointment.
Captures the interpreter assignment status for an appointment, indicating whether an interpreter has been assigned or not assigned.
The ID number associated with the inpatient episode of care, which encompasses discharges from the ED.
Indicates if the patient encounter is a walk-in. A value of Y signifies that the encounter is a walk-in, while a null or N indicates it is not a walk-in.
The date of the patient's LAST_MENSTRUAL_PERIOD. This data is available only for encounters involving female patients.

The initial Level of Service modifier assigned to the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The second LEVEL_OF_SERVICE_MODIFIER associated with the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The third LEVEL_OF_SERVICE_MODIFIER applied to the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The fourth LEVEL_OF_SERVICE_MODIFIER associated with the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The ID of the procedure record associated with the primary LOS_CODE for this encounter. This is not the CPT_CODE and serves as an internal identifier that is generally not accessible to users.

A flag that indicates if the appointment is for a service not included in the patient's coverage benefits. It is marked as "Y" when the service is not covered and "N" when it is covered.
The unique identifier for the ordering provider associated with an appointment, as recorded on the Orders form within the Appointment Info activity.
Data from a free text field that includes details about the provider who submitted the order.

Specifies if a call related to a telephone encounter was made by the patient or the clinic/hospital. A "Y" denotes an outgoing call from the clinic/hospital, while an "N" signifies an incoming call from the patient.

A unique contact date represented in decimal format. The unique identifier for the provider record of the patient's General Primary Care Provider at the time of the encounter. This ID may be encrypted if the security utility for enterprise reporting has been selected.
This represents the status provided by an automated appointment reminder system, with typical values including CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, BUSY, etc. This item is configured by batch templates 91 and 96.

When this flag is enabled, it prevents all phone calls associated with this appointment. The phone number designated for receiving all calls related to this appointment.

Instructions for entering charges related to this procedure.
Time required for cleanup after this procedure.

ID of the logical deployment owner associated with this record. Logical owners indicate the deployment in which the record was created, but do not reflect whether the record is affected by version skew.
ID of the physical deployment owner associated with this record. Physical owners indicate the location where the data is hosted, either on the cross-over server or the owner deployment.
Specifies if concurrency should be calculated for this procedure.

Specifies whether the user has permission to modify the description.

Moment of modification or creation.

This item defines the lookback period for checking duplicates, storing the interval as a string value in days. Indicates the active status of the procedure code. Shows "Y" for active and "N" for inactive.
Indicates whether the billing system should apply the payment or adjustment to the bad debt balance. This applies solely to payments and credit adjustments.

*** Deprecated *** This column is no longer in use and does not retrieve any data. For reporting on responses to appointment questionnaires, refer to the table PATIENT_ENC_QNRS_ANS.

APPT_SERIAL_NO is a non-unique serial number assigned to the appointment, which typically matches the ENCOUNTER_ID unless the appointment is canceled and rescheduled. In such instances, the APPT_SERIAL_NO for the rescheduled appointment remains the same as the original appointment, but the ENCOUNTER_IDs will differ.
The category value representing the appointment status of the encounter based on the latest enterprise reporting extract, including values like 1 – Scheduled, 2 – Completed, 3 – Canceled, etc.
The date intended for scheduling the appointment.
The date and time of the scheduled appointment for the encounter is recorded in a twenty-four hour format, for example, 1 P.M. on January 4, 2000, is represented as 01/04/2000 13:00.

The date and time when the encounter was removed from the arrival list. NOTE: This column will first attempt to retrieve data from the ARRIVAL LIST DELETE WHEN item (EPT 7233), and if no data is found, it will then pull from AUDITED INSTANT (EPT 7544).

The unique identifier of the system user who deleted the encounter from the arrival list. This ID may be encrypted and will first attempt to retrieve data from the ARRIVAL LIST DELETE BY WHOM item (EPT 7234); if no data is found, it will then source from AUDITED USER ID (EPT 7543).

In the PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS table, the column AR_EPISODE_ID (EPT,2208) has been deprecated. The data for this deprecated column is no longer accessible as it is not being populated in the source system.
Indicates the type of interpreter assigned to an appointment. This value should be empty if the assignment status is empty, "Not Needed," or "Needs Review.
The unique identifier for the attending provider.
UNIQUE_ID of the user who initially prints the After Visit Summary (AVS) for the encounter.
The moment when the After Visit Summary (AVS) was generated for this encounter.
Holds the COMPONENT or COMPONENT_GROUP utilized to locate the ADJUDICATION_TABLE during the copay adjudication process.
Holds the benefit package utilized for copay calculations.
Holds the adjudicated copy amount for the visit based on the patient's coverage benefits.
Holds the Adjudication Formula that is utilized to calculate the copay.
Indicator showing whether the adjudicated copay was overridden and the method of the override.
Holds the Adjudication Table utilized for calculating the copay.
Holds the adjudicated self-pay amount (the amount the patient must pay) used to calculate the copay amount for the visit.
This represents the patient's BODY_MASS_INDEX, calculated using the documented HEIGHT and WEIGHT.
The diastolic component of the patient's blood pressure recorded during this encounter.
The systolic component of the patient's blood pressure recorded during this encounter.
This represents the patient's BODY_SURFACE_AREA, calculated using the documented height and weight.

A status flag that indicates whether to include data from the ENCOUNTER in the SlicerDicer reporting application. The statuses are 1-Possible (e.g., the encounter is a scheduled outpatient appointment or the admission is pending) or 2-Complete (e.g., the appointment is complete, the admission is discharged).
The free text provided in the COMMENT field when an appointment is canceled.
The category number for the reason a patient encounter was canceled.
Holds the Certification that was active for the encounter department during the time of the encounter.

The ENCOUNTER_FORM_NUMBER or charge slip number assigned to this encounter. Note: The charge slip number is also recorded in the financial table TRANSACTION_DETAIL, allowing for linkage to TRANSACTION_DETAIL to identify financial transactions related to the encounter.

The CHECKIN_DTTM represents the date and time when the patient checked in for the appointment related to this encounter. The date is always the appointment date, irrespective of the actual check-in date, and the time can be adjusted by users, which may differ from the system-audited time; for the system-recorded check-in time, refer to the CHECKIN_AUD_DTTM column in PATIENT_ENC_7.
The unique identifier for the system user who checked in the patient for this encounter. This field will be NULL if the encounter has not undergone the Check In process, and the ID may be encrypted.

The CHECKOUT_DTTM indicates the date and time the patient was checked out for this encounter, with the date always reflecting the appointment date, irrespective of the actual check-out date. The time can be adjusted by users in the application, which may not necessarily align with the system-audited time; for the system-recorded check-out time, refer to the CHECKOUT_AUD_DTTM column in PATIENT_ENC_7.
The Kiosk where the appointment is checked in.
The category number for the visit indicator associated with this patient encounter.
The date linked to the visit indicator as recorded by a system user during Check In.
The unique identifier for the billing system Claim record (CLM record) that is associated with charges for this visit.
Identifier for the deployment owner associated with this contact.
This item indicates the type of consent recorded for a specific encounter. It is a single-response category defined by the customer.
Comments made by the provider regarding the contact.
The date of this contact presented in a calendar format.

The value in the COPAY_COLLECTED field represents the amount entered by the user during Check In. If the facility utilizes the Registration or POS copay form, multiple copays may be collected per appointment, but this field only shows the last copay collected. Comprehensive data on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the AR copay form is used, this is the appropriate data source.

The dollar amount displayed in the COPAY_DUE field during the Check In Patient activity of the scheduling system. This amount can be either calculated by the system based on the patient's coverage benefit information or manually input by a user. The field may also be blank if no copay amount was provided at the time of the patient's check-in.
The method used to pay the copay for an appointment (e.g., through MYCHART, a kiosk).

The COPAY_PAYMENT_EXPLANATION_CATEGORY_NUMBER for this patient encounter. This field is populated only if the facility utilizes the POS copay form during check-in/check-out. Users may collect multiple copays per appointment, but this field reflects only the last copay collected for that appointment. Information on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table.

The reference number for the copay associated with this encounter during Check In, which may be a check number or credit card number. Note: If the facility utilizes the Registration or POS copay form at check-in/check-out, multiple copays may be collected per appointment, but this field only shows the last copay collected for that appointment. Information on all copays collected can be accessed in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the AR copay form is used, this is the appropriate data source.

The COPAY_SOURCE_CATEGORY_NUMBER indicates the copay source for the patient encounter. It is important to note that if the facility utilizes the Registration or POS copay form during check-in/check-out, multiple copays may be collected per appointment; however, this field only shows the last copay collected. Comprehensive data on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the AR copay form is used, this is the appropriate data source.

The COPAY_TYPE_CATEGORY_NUMBER indicates the category of copay for the patient encounter. It is important to note that if the facility utilizes the Registration or POS copay form during check-in/check-out, multiple copays may be collected per appointment; however, this field only shows the last copay collected for that appointment. Information on all copays collected is available in the PATIENT_ENC_COPAY_COLL table, and if the facility uses the AR copay form, this is the appropriate data source.
The ID number of the COVERAGE_RECORD associated with the visit at the time of scheduling or check-in. This ID may be encrypted.
This represents the name of the user who initiated the encounter.
The ID of the department associated with the encounter. If the encounter involves multiple departments, this ID corresponds to the first department in the list.
The date when the encounter was discharged.
DOWNTIME_ENCOUNTER_IDENTIFIER refers to a unique identifier for an encounter that is associated with downtime.
The kiosk workstation that handled the ED arrival.

The ENCOUNTER_DATE represents the date of the encounter, which varies based on the contact type. For surgery encounters, the date of the surgery is returned; for Hospital encounters, the appropriate date is derived from Admission/Discharge/Transfer (ADT) information. If ADT information is unavailable, the Hospital Admission date (I EPT 18850) is returned, and if that is also not found, the temporary admission date (I EPT 18846) will be provided.

The start date and time of an encounter is derived from the date in the EFFECTIVE_DATE_DT column. The time is taken from the earliest populated entry among the following fields: hospital admission time (EPT 18851), hospital temporary admission time (EPT 18847), ADT arrival time (EPT 10815), and expected admission time (EPT 10300). The SlicerDicer reporting application utilizes this column to establish the EffectiveStartDate of encounters.

The effective department ID is determined by identifying the first department with a value in the following sequence: 1) HOSPITAL_UNIT 2) PROCEDURE_PASS_DEPARTMENT (the effective department of the associated appointment or admission) 3) HOSPICE_INTAKE_DEPARTMENT 4) APPOINTMENT_DEPARTMENT.
A unique serial number assigned to this encounter, which is distinct for all patients and encounters within the system.

A flag indicating whether the encounter is closed at the time of the enterprise reporting extract. The column can contain the values Y, N, or null, where null signifies that closing the encounter is not applicable, such as in the case of a future appointment.
The unique identifier for the system user who concluded the patient encounter. This identifier may be encrypted.
The date when the patient encounter was concluded.
This column records the time when the encounter was concluded.
The ID number of the user who created the PATIENT or ENCOUNTER record.
The moment an ENCOUNTER was initiated.
The category value for the reason for freezing the encounter medication.
The category number for the encounter type associated with the encounter.
The title of the encounter type for the encounter.
Holds the legal owning entity for the ENCOUNTER_DEPARTMENT during the encounter.
The timestamp indicating when this patient contact was created. This column is utilized for executing standard EMR validations against the source system.
Status of orders within the scheduling system.
The ID for the contact assigned by a non-system, typically filled in through an interface.
The category value linked to the Financial Class of the encounter. Note: This item is populated solely through an interface and will not be populated if a billing system is installed.

The patient's HEAD_CIRCUMFERENCE as documented during this encounter. This field will only contain data for patients younger than the age defined in Miscellaneous Configuration. Note: This value is recorded in centimeters.
The height of the patient documented during this encounter. This field is a string and may include indicators for feet and/or inches.
The ID number associated with the hospital billing account for the encounter.
The date and time when the patient was initially admitted to the facility, placed in a bed in the ED, or confirmed for an HOV during this contact, irrespective of the patient's base patient class.
The category value indicating the type of admission for this encounter.
The date and time of discharge from the hospital for this patient contact.
Holds the Hospital License that was valid for the encounter department during the time of the encounter.
The ID number of the record that specifies the storage method for inpatient data related to the encounter.
Holds the name of the interpreter designated for an appointment when the interpreter lacks a provider record (i.e., assigned from an external source).
A flag that indicates if a patient needs an interpreter for an encounter.
This value represents the identifier of the vendor supplying the interpreter for the appointment.
Captures the interpreter assignment status for an appointment, indicating whether an interpreter has been assigned or not assigned.
The ID number associated with the inpatient episode of care, which encompasses discharges from the ED.
Indicates if the patient encounter is a walk-in. A value of Y signifies that the encounter is a walk-in, while a null or N indicates it is not a walk-in.
The date of the patient's LAST_MENSTRUAL_PERIOD. This data is available only for encounters involving female patients.
The column LMP_OTHER_CODE in the PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS table is deprecated and has been replaced by the OBGYN_STAT_C column in the V_OB_ENC_OBGYN_STAT table.
The initial Level of Service modifier assigned to the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The second LEVEL_OF_SERVICE_MODIFIER associated with the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The third LEVEL_OF_SERVICE_MODIFIER applied to the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The fourth LEVEL_OF_SERVICE_MODIFIER associated with the encounter. This field will be blank if no modifier exists.
The ID of the procedure record associated with the primary LOS_CODE for this encounter. This is not the CPT_CODE and serves as an internal identifier that is generally not accessible to users.
The procedure code associated with the primary LOS (level of service).
A flag that indicates if the appointment is for a service not included in the patient's coverage benefits. It is marked as "Y" when the service is not covered and "N" when it is covered.
The unique identifier for the ordering provider associated with an appointment, as recorded on the Orders form within the Appointment Info activity.
Data from a free text field that includes details about the provider who submitted the order.

Specifies if a call related to a telephone encounter was made by the patient or the clinic/hospital. A "Y" denotes an outgoing call from the clinic/hospital, while an "N" signifies an incoming call from the patient.

A unique contact date represented in decimal format. The integer part indicates the date of contact, while the digits following the decimal point differentiate multiple contacts on the same date, with each contact being unique; for instance, .00 represents the first or only contact, .01 represents the second contact, and so on.
The unique identifier assigned to the patient record. This ID may be encrypted if the use of the enterprise reporting encryption utility has been selected.

The unique identifier for the provider record of the patient's General Primary Care Provider at the time of the encounter. This ID may be encrypted if the security utility for enterprise reporting has been selected.
This represents the status provided by an automated appointment reminder system, with typical values including CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, BUSY, etc. This item is configured by batch templates 91 and 96.

When this flag is enabled, it prevents all phone calls associated with this appointment. A null value in this column signifies that no user had the option to block a phone call for this contact, which may be due to: (a) the contact not being an appointment, (b) the appointment being created prior to the introduction of this feature, or (c) the department not utilizing the standard Appointment Demographics node in its After Appointment Entry Advantage Activity.
The phone number designated for receiving all calls related to this appointment.
The unique identifier for the patient's primary location at the time of the encounter. Note: This may differ from the patient's current primary location.
The PULSE measurement of the patient recorded during this encounter.
The unique identifier for the referral record associated with this appointment.
A flag that indicates if a referral is necessary for an appointment based on visit coverage. It is marked as “Y” when a referral is required and “N” when it is not.
The REFERRAL_ID number of the referring physician, who may belong to an external organization.
The RESPIRATION_RATE of the patient as noted during this encounter.

A flag indicating whether the routing summary was printed at the time of the enterprise reporting extract. This column can have a value of Y (printed) or N (not printed), with the default value set to N.
The connection to the SERVICE_AREA for the ENCOUNTER.

The date and time when the patient checked in for the appointment related to this encounter. The date is always the appointment date, irrespective of the actual check-in date, and the time can be adjusted by users in the application, which may differ from the system-audited time. For the system-recorded check-in time, refer to the SIGNIN_AUD_DTTM column in PATIENT_ENC_7.
The unique identifier of the system user who signed in the patient for this encounter. This field will be NULL if the encounter has not undergone the Sign In process, and the ID may be encrypted.
The category value related to the surgical service for this patient contact.
The temperature of the patient recorded during this encounter. This value is expressed in degrees Fahrenheit, irrespective of the method used to enter the temperature reading.

In the PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS table, the TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG column is no longer in use and has been replaced by the TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG column in the PATIENT_ENC4 table. To retrieve the value of the deprecated column after the EMR system upgrade, join PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS.TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG with PATIENT_ENC4.TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG.
The timestamp when this patient encounter was included in enterprise reporting.

This column is populated solely for indemnity coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 1) and contains the unique identifier of the payor linked to the coverage record. For managed care coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 2), join COVERAGE.COVERAGE_ID with V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.COVERAGE_ID and apply filters on V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.EFF_DATE and V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.TERM_DATE to retrieve the corresponding PAYOR_ID.

This column is populated solely for indemnity coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 1) and contains the unique identifier for the benefit plan linked to the coverage record. For managed care coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 2), join COVERAGE.COVERAGE_ID with V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.COVERAGE_ID and apply filters on V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.EFF_DATE and V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.TERM_DATE to identify the corresponding BENEFIT_PLAN_ID.

The financial class associated with this coverage is utilized solely for CMS claims forms and may not be consistently populated for reporting purposes. Reporting should be conducted using the financial class of the payor indicated in this coverage.

The unique identifier for the visit provider linked to this encounter. If multiple providers are associated with one encounter, this ID refers to the first provider in the list. This item may be NULL if no provider is present for this encounter, and the ID may be encrypted.
The title of the visit provider (SER 5). Refer to VISIT_PROV_ID above for the definition of visit provider.
This field records any specific requirements for a visit.
Comments regarding the expected account type are stored in EPT 2245.
A field that specifies if the patient's contact pertains to a workers compensation or third party liability case.
The patient's weight recorded during this encounter is stored in ounces, regardless of the input method. To convert this value to pounds, divide the number by 16.
The SERIAL_NUMBER for the bed contact in the event record is unique to all bed contacts within the system.
The ID number associated with the bed in the event record for the duration of the effective time span.
A unique identifier for a bed that combines the name and the bed ID. This column is commonly utilized for grouping, sorting, and displaying information in reports.
The ID number representing the department associated with the event record at the time it is effective.
The name associated with the department.
A unique identifier for a department that combines the name and the department ID. This column is frequently utilized for grouping, sorting, and displaying data in reports.
The unique identifier for the location that acts as the parent to the department within the facility's ADT organizational structure.
The name associated with the ADT_LOCATION.
A unique identifier for a location that combines the name and the LOCATION_ID. This column is commonly utilized for grouping, sorting, and displaying information in reports.
The SERIAL_NUMBER for the room contact associated with the event record. This number is unique among all room contacts in the system.
The ID number of the room associated with the event record within the valid time period.
A unique identifier for a room that combines the name and the room ID. This column is commonly utilized for grouping, sorting, and displaying information in reports.
The unique identifier for the service area associated with this location.
The designation of the service area.
A unique identifier for a service area that combines the name and the service area ID. This column is commonly utilized for grouping, sorting, and displaying information in reports.

The unique identifier for this contact's encounter. This number is distinct for all patient encounters within the system. If IntraConnect is utilized, this corresponds to the Unique Contact Identifier (UCI).
The unique identifier for the ADT_EVENT record.
The CATEGORY value that indicates the type of the event record.
The moment the patient was transferred to the department/room/bed.
The column PATIENT_OUT_DTTM indicates the moment the patient was transferred out of the department/room/bed. If the patient remains in the department/room/bed, this column will not provide a value.

This column records the exact moment the patient was transferred out of the department/room/bed. If the patient remains in the department/room/bed, this column will not contain any value, while the column OUT_DTTM will show the time of transfer or the current time if the patient is still present.

The unique ID of the order event action record associated with this dispense. This record documents the history of actions taken in Dispense Queue, Dispense Preparation, Dispense Checking, and Dispense Tracking, and is often used to connect to the V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE_ACTION view.
This column records the count of "Barcode Not Recognized" warnings (warning type 35014) linked to this dispense, excluding any duplicate warnings.
The unique internal contact date associated with the dispense contact for this order dispense. This column is often utilized to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.

The unique identifier for the department to which this dispense was sent. Typically, this corresponds to the patient's department at the time of the action; however, if the dispense was directed to a different department, such as a surgical unit, that department's ID is recorded.
The category number associated with the MEDICATION_DISPENSE_CODE.
The initial line of the comment provided by the user who declined the dispense during the dispense check.
The explanation provided for the rejection of the dispense during the dispense check.

This column represents the category ID for the dispense check status of the dispense. It indicates whether the order underwent a dispense check and if any warnings were encountered during that process, and it is often used to connect to the ZC_DISP_CHECK_STAT table.
The linked dispense contact created due to the rejection of the initial dispense contact.
The identifier for the medication dispense code associated with this dispense.
The date when the item was dispensed.
The date and time when the dispense occurred.
The hour of the day when the dispense occurs.

This column contains a value of 1 if the dispense preparation was initiated but not finished in the Dispense Preparation activity; otherwise, it holds a value of 0. A dispense is deemed started if either of the following warnings appeared during preparation: 35016 - "Dispense Prep Order Discontinued or Completed" or 35017 - "Dispense Prep Order Past End Time.
This column contains a value of 1 if the dispense was successfully completed during the Dispense Preparation activity; otherwise, it contains a value of 0.
The date when the dispense was prepared during the Dispense Preparation activity or in an external system.
The date and time when the dispense was prepared during the Dispense Preparation activity or in an external system.
The hour of the day when the dispense was prepared during the Dispense Preparation activity or by an external system.

This column shows if the dispense preparation included a near miss. A near miss is identified when a warning triggers, prompting the user to cancel and restart the action. The warning types evaluated for near misses are: 35010 - Dispense Prep NDC Not Part of Order and 35011 - Dispense Prep NDC Expired.

This column contains a value of 0 if a dispense was either prepared or attempted during the Dispense Preparation activity, or if dispense preparation data was obtained from an external system. If neither condition is met, it holds a value of 1.
The unique identifier for the user linked to the order event action record.
This column contains "Y" if the dispense contact has a return contact that references it, and "N" if it does not. A partial return is treated as a return.
The number representing the category of the dispense type.
The unique identifier for the user who performed this dispense.

This column contains the count of warnings related to "NDC Expired", "CNR Expired", "NDC Expiring Soon", and "CNR Expiring Soon" (warning types 35011, 35013, 35050, or 35052) for this dispense, excluding any duplicate warnings.

The CATEGORY_VALUE of the general dispense type of the dispense is determined by the actual dispense type and several other factors, including the pharmacy type and order attributes. This column is often used to connect to the ZC_GEN_DISP_TYPE table.
This column contains a value of 1 if the dispense was modified by an interface message from an external dispense preparation system; otherwise, it holds a value of 0.

The unique internal contact date for the most recent receive action in the Dispense Tracking activity. This column, along with ACTION_ID, is commonly used to connect to the V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE_ACTION view.

The unique internal contact date of the most recent action sent in the Dispense Tracking activity. This column, along with ACTION_ID, is commonly used to connect to the V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE_ACTION view.
The ID of the location linked to the pharmacy that is responsible for this dispense.
The name of the location linked to the pharmacy that is responsible for this dispense.
This column contains the count of manually linked ingredients for the warning types "NDC Not Part of Order" and "CNR Doesn't Match Order" (35010 or 35012) related to this dispense.

This column contains the unique ID of the medication that is the dispensable product for the order. It is commonly used to reference the MEDICATIONS table, and in the case of IMS, it selects the medication record assessed for IMS instead of the IMS mixture template; manually bulk charged orders will have a value of NULL.
The name assigned to the medication.
This column indicates the total count of NDCs that were entered manually for this dispense.
The unique identifier for the medication order.
This column contains "Y" when the dispense is pending and "N" otherwise.
The ID of the PHARMACY that is accountable for this dispense.
The name of the PHARMACY that is accountable for this dispense.
The designation of the pharmacy's physical type.

Indicates the physical type of the pharmacy, which may include options such as Standard Inpatient Pharmacy, Automated Dispensing System, Robotic Dispensing System, Pill Counter, etc. The default value is Standard.
This column contains the count of "NDC Not Part of Order" and "CNR Doesn't Match Order" warnings (warning types 35010, 35012, or 35059) related to this dispense, excluding any duplicate warnings.
This column contains "Y" if the dispense had an overridden alert for either "NDC Not Part of Order" or "Compound Not Part of Order" during preparation; otherwise, it contains "N".
The date when the action occurred. This column should be utilized for date ranges to facilitate efficient searches.
The distinct internal contact date associated with the dispense's order event record.
The date and time when the action took place.
The hour of the day represented by ACTION_DTTM.
The unique identifier for the dispense's action order event record. This column is commonly used to join with F_RX_DISPENSE.ACTION_ID.
The distinct contact number associated with this order event action contact.
The category number for the action type related to the order event action. This category information can be found in the ZC_ACTION_TYPE_2 table.
The designation of the action type executed during a dispense.
The name of the container utilized to transmit the dose linked to the ORDER_EVENT_ACTION_RECORD.
The identifier for the sending method utilized to transmit the dose to a floor or patient during a dispense tracking action.
The SENDING_METHOD_CATEGORY_ID indicates the method used to send the dose linked to the order event action record.
The unique identifier for the department where a medication dose is administered during the Dispense Tracking activity.
The name of the department that administered the dose for a dispense tracking action.
The unique identifier for the user linked to the order event action record.
Indicates whether this order was processed using an override.

This column shows if the ADS override is associated with a clinical order. A "Y" signifies it is linked, while an "N" indicates it is not linked; no value will be returned if the order is not an ADS override.
The provider who authorizes the order, typically associated with the PROVIDERS table.
Specifies whether this order is part of the bulk charge activity.
Indicates whether the order is conditional. A conditional order will not be initiated until the patient meets a specified set of criteria after it has been released.
The minimum quantity of the medication that can be ordered, as indicated by the user in the orders activity.
The category number associated with the route of administration for a medication.
The measurement unit for the prescribed dose.
The CATEGORY_NUMBER for the dose unit of a medication.

The unique identifier for the encounter associated with the order. This number is distinct for all patient encounters. If using IntraConnect, this corresponds to the Unique Contact Identifier (UCI). This column is frequently utilized to join with the PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS table.

The unique internal contact date for the first administration contact related to the order. This date reflects the first contact based on the recorded time, rather than when the documentation was completed, and is often used to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.

The line number for the information related to the MAR action that established the first administration contact, FIRST_ADMIN_DATE_REAL. Only actions that create administration contacts and indicate a patient receiving medication (MED_ADMIN_RECORDS.MAR_ACTION_CODE is 1-Given, 6-New Bag, 12-Bolus, 13-Push, or custom actions mapped to these) are considered. This column is commonly used to connect to the MED_ADMIN_RECORDS table.
The unique internal date of the first dispense contact for the order. This column is often utilized to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.
The unique internal contact date for the initial pend verify contact associated with the order. This column is often utilized to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.
The initial scheduled due time for the medication order. If modified during order verification, it is updated to reflect the new date and time.
The unique internal date of the first verification contact for the order. This column is often used to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.

The line number for the data related to the most recent action in the verification queue during the order verification process. If the order has been verified, this represents the verification audit trail associated with FIRST_VERIFY_DATE_REAL and is often used to connect to the RX_VERIFY_TRACE table.
The unique identifier for the discrete frequency record related to this medication order. This column is commonly used to connect to the IP_FREQUENCY table.
The designation of the order frequency.
This column records the date and time when a conditional order was initiated.
This indicates if an order has been released. Unreleased orders lack a report date, so when using the REPORT_DATE column for a date range, signed and held orders will be automatically excluded.
Specifies if an intervention has been recorded for this order. A "Y" signifies that at least one intervention is documented, while an "N" indicates that no interventions are recorded.

The unique internal contact date of the most recent verification contact for the order initiated by a user. This date pertains to the last verification contact where MEDICATION_ORDERS.MED_VERIFY_TYPE_CODE is not 4-Modify On Patient Transfer, 5-Modify On Order Transfer, or 6-NDC replacement. This column is often used to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table for details on changes made to orders that have undergone reverification. The last verification contact, irrespective of verify type, is available in ORDER_RXVER_NOADSN.LAST_VERIFY_DATE_REAL.

Columns with Medication IDs in MEDICATION_ORDERS and its related addendum tables may include Orderable records or templates that do not correspond to actual medications. It is advisable to utilize this column for reporting on medication orders, and if your search involves mixture components, ensure to also query ORDER_MEDMIXINFO.MEDICATION_ID alongside this column.
The name assigned to the medication.

Indicates if a medication order has been confirmed by the pharmacist as non-formulary. A "Y" signifies that the pharmacist has verified the order as non-formulary. To identify orders placed as non-formulary, refer to the NF_PRE_VERIFY_FLAG column. A NULL value indicates that the order was either rejected or not verified.
Indicates if the order was submitted as non-formulary before verification. A "Y" signifies a non-formulary medication.
This column indicates whether the order was a non-clinical override in the case of an ADS override. Non-clinical overrides result in charge-only orders that are not displayed on the MAR.
Indicates if the ORDER is a one-step medication, meaning its administration is recorded in a single step.

This indicates whether a medication order is made on-the-fly by nurses. An on-the-fly medication order is created by scanning an NDC, as opposed to an ADS override, which involves pulling a drug from an ADS cabinet to generate a new order interface message.

This column contains the medication ID of the Orderable record if a medication was ordered using an IMS orderable for Mixtures or Drips. It is primarily intended for searching the usage of specific Orderables.
The date associated with ORDERING_DTTM.
The unique internal contact date for the ordering contact associated with the order. This column is often utilized to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.

The date and time when the order was released. For other order types created on the fly, such as override pulls, one step medications, and bulk charges, this represents the time the order was created.
The hour of the day represented by ORDERING_DTTM.
The unique identifier for the provider who issued the medication order, typically associated with the PROVIDERS table.
The specific dose of a medication input by the user during the orders activity.
The END_DATE_TIME of the order.
A reference to the Order History activity for the EMR system-Crystal Integration, represented as RX_ORDER_NM_WID.
The unique identifier for the medication order.
The name of the category for the order priority.
The category number indicating the priority level assigned to an order.
The sequence in which the route of administration is applied.
The date and time when the order was initiated.

The unique identifier for the patient department at the time the order was issued. For override pulls and bulk charges, this corresponds to the dispense department of the order. If the order's department is unavailable, the department from the order's encounter is utilized instead (PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS.EFFECTIVE_DEPT_ID).
The name of the patient department when the order was issued. For override pulls, this refers to the dispense department associated with the order.
The unique identifier for the patient record associated with this line. This column is often utilized to connect to the PATIENTS table.
The unique identifier for the revenue location associated with the patient department when the order was generated or released.
The name of the revenue location associated with the patient department when the order was either released or created.
This indicates if a frequency is classified as PRN (as needed).
The name of the final queue reason. The potential values are detailed in the description for RXQ_REASON_CODE.
The user responsible for releasing the order.

The date when the order was released; for conditional orders, this represents the initiation time. If the conditional order was not initiated, the value is null. This column is often utilized as a date range in reports.

The CATEGORY_ID of the last reason the order entered the verify queue during the initial order verification process. Possible values include 1-New, 11-Override Pull, 15-First Verify, 16-2nd Verify, 17-Conditional, 18-Conditional 1rst, 19-Conditional 2nd, 20-Conditional Initiate, 23-Review On-The-Fly, or 25-Deferred.
The ORDER_NAME is derived from multiple potential sources, prioritized as follows: DISPLAY_NAME, ORDER_DESCRIPTION, and lastly, the MEDICATION_NAME.
A unique identifier for an order formed by combining RX_ORDER_NAME and the order ID. This column is frequently utilized for grouping, sorting, and presentation in reports.
The CATEGORY_ID of the last unqueue reason or action performed by a user during the initial order verification process, which may be 1-Verified or 2-Rejected.
The identifier for the most recent unqueue action taken by a user in the initial order verification process. The potential values are detailed in the description for RX_UNQUEUE_REAS_CODE.
The date associated with VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DTTM.
The date and time when the order was placed in the verify queue for the reason specified in QUEUE_REASON.
The hour of the day for the column VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DTTM.
This item contains the login department of the user who is verifying, which is stored in ORD 48018.
The user who performed the action that resulted in the order being removed from the verify queue.
The date associated with VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DTTM.
The date and time when the user performed the action that led to the unqueue reason specified in UNQUEUE_REASON.
The hour component of VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DTTM.
